output:
**What I found:** Only the retry wrapper should move down. Replace `src/lib/retry.ts` with `got` 14's built-in `retry` option, which moves the code from our custom code to a library the `got` maintainers own (the record calls this `L4 CODE -> L3 LIB`). The discount function encodes our own policy and would stay with the same team, so moving it into `src/shared/` is not a bring-down; it goes to the architecture skills.

**Why it matters:** `got` does not retry POST by default, and POST retries caused both production incidents. Keeping the wrapper means we keep maintaining a 140-line file that took six fixes last quarter.

**Do this first:**
1. Move one real outbound client from `src/lib/retry.ts` onto `got`'s `retry` option, then delete the wrapper call for that client.
2. Move the other consumers, delete `src/lib/retry.ts`, and add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` ban on that path.
3. Hand the `isEligibleForDiscount` merge to `morphogenetic-architecture` and `architecture-guidelines`.

**What I did not check:**
- The source: there is no `src/` or `package.json` in the working directory, so everything below rests on your description. To close this, run `rg -n "retry" src/lib/retry.ts` and `rg -n "retry:\s*\{?\s*limit:\s*0|retry:\s*0" src` in the repo.
- That the installed `got` really is 14.x: `npm ls got`.
- That the wrapper's backoff timing matches `got`'s default. I checked `got`'s behaviour from memory of the v14 docs and did not browse; confirm against `got`'s `documentation/7-retry.md`.

---

```
Scope:          One Node.js 22 TypeScript API repo, one team of four; src/lib/retry.ts and
                three copies of isEligibleForDiscount
Mode:           Assessment
Decision:       Bring down src/lib/retry.ts to got 14's native retry option (L4 CODE -> L3 LIB).
                No bring-down for isEligibleForDiscount; hand off.
Summary:        The retry wrapper is generic retry logic with no domain content. It duplicates a
                feature of a library that is already approved and already handles every outbound
                call, and two production incidents came from a bug that got's defaults avoid
                (retrying non-idempotent POST). The discount copies are our own business policy
                and the proposed destination has the same owner, so this skill excludes it. Key
                risk: a call site that relies on the wrapper's current method list or timing
                changes behaviour when the wrapper goes.

Candidates:
- src/lib/retry.ts (140-line exponential-backoff wrapper around got calls)
  - Move: L4 CODE -> L3 LIB (distance 1)
  - Landing: got 14 `retry` request option (limit, methods, statusCodes, errorCodes,
    maxRetryAfter, backoffLimit, noise, calculateDelay), set once through got.extend() and
    overridable per request
  - Owners: our team -> got maintainers (sindresorhus/got); approved by the platform team
  - Evidence: six bug-fix commits in one quarter; two production incidents from retrying
    non-idempotent POST; got's default `methods` leaves POST out and its default backoff is
    exponential with jitter; the wrapper has no domain-specific behaviour
  - Variation: none reported. Any call site that intentionally retries a POST must opt in
    per request, for example with an idempotency key. That opt-in is the escape hatch and
    does not block the move.
  - Confidence: High (Medium until the wrapper's behaviour is diffed against got's defaults)
  - Next action: Write down the wrapper's limit, methods, codes, and delay formula. Create
    one got.extend({ retry: {...} }) instance with matching settings, minus POST. Move one
    consumer onto it and confirm with a test that a failing POST is not retried and a
    failing GET is.

Priorities:
1. src/lib/retry.ts -> got native retry
   - Why now: high churn (six fixes in one quarter), real damage (two incidents from
     duplicate POSTs), approved landing already installed, migration effort small
   - Move: L4 CODE -> L3 LIB
   - Landing: got 14 `retry` option through got.extend()
   - Migration proof: one production outbound client moved and its retry test passing
   - Retire: delete src/lib/retry.ts and every `retry: { limit: 0 }` override; add an
     ESLint no-restricted-imports rule on the old path

Gaps:
- Exact wrapper behaviour (attempt limit, status and error codes, delay cap) not seen; only
  described
- Whether any caller depends on POST retries (it would need an idempotency key, see
  concurrency-control)
- Whether the wrapper emits logs or metrics that callers consume; got exposes
  hooks.beforeRetry for that

Handoffs:
- isEligibleForDiscount (three identical 40-line copies -> src/shared/discount.ts)
  - Reason excluded: same owner (this team maintains both the source and the
    destination), the logic is our own domain policy, and src/shared/ is a repo-local
    shared module. No external landing applies.
  - Better skill: morphogenetic-architecture (decide which domain owns the discount policy;
    src/shared/ may be the wrong home for business rules), architecture-guidelines
    (pure-function core), architecture-as-code (ban new local copies once merged). The
    merge itself is reasonable: three identical copies of one policy will drift.
```
